1972.description: Original Act providing for protection of wild animals, birds and plants. Established basic framework: hunting prohibition (Section 9), protected areas (sanctuaries, national parks), trade regulation, penalties.
keyChanges: Established hunting prohibition for Schedule I-IV species
Created sanctuary and national park framework
Regulated trade in wild animals, articles, trophies
Established Chief Wild Life Warden system
Defined penalties (original: up to 3 years, ₹2,000)
Six Schedules (I-VI) for species/plant listing
1972.impact: Foundation of wildlife law in India. First comprehensive wildlife protection legislation.

1982.description: Minor amendments mainly to definitions and procedural aspects.
keyChanges: Amended definition of 'animal' to include amphibians
Modified provisions relating to licences and permits
Clarified certain procedural aspects

1986.description: Major amendment introducing Chapter VA - prohibition of trade in scheduled animals (Schedule I and Part II of Schedule II). Added ivory import dealers to licensing. Peacock feather trade exemption.
keyChanges: INSERTED Chapter VA (Sections 49A-49C): Complete trade ban on scheduled animals
Defined 'scheduled animal' = Schedule I or Part II of Schedule II
Specified date concept: 2 months from commencement/addition to schedule
Prohibited manufacture, taxidermy, dealing in scheduled animal articles
Added ivory import dealers to licensing (Section 44)
Exempted peacock feather manufacturers/dealers
Government corporations exempted for export purposes
Enhanced penalties: Section 51A (1-7 years, ₹5,000+) for Chapter VA offences
Declaration requirements for existing stock (Section 49C)
1986.impact: First major trade ban. Addressed ivory trade. Established 'scheduled animal' concept. Foundation for later CITES implementation.

1991.description: Comprehensive amendment - renamed Act, added Chapter IIIA (specified plants), Chapter IVA (Central Zoo Authority), strengthened penalties, redefined schedules.
keyChanges: RENAMED Act long title: 'protection of wild animals, birds and plants'
INSERTED Chapter IIIA (Sections 17A-17H): Protection of Specified Plants (Schedule VI)
INSERTED Chapter IVA (Sections 38A-38J): Central Zoo Authority and Recognition of Zoos
Redefined 'animal' to include amphibians, birds, mammals, reptiles, young and eggs
Redefined 'hunting' to include capturing, coursing, snaring, trapping, driving, baiting
Redefined 'wild animal' = Schedules I-IV (was I-V)
Redefined 'vermin' = notified under Section 62
Omitted Schedule V (vermin schedule), moved vermin to Section 62 notification
Enhanced penalties: Section 51 - up to 3 years, ₹25,000 (was ₹2,000)
Section 51A: Strict bail conditions for Schedule I/II offences
Section 54: Compounding up to ₹25,000
Zoo regulation: Recognition mandatory, standards for housing/upkeep
Specified plant protection: prohibition on picking, uprooting, trade
Central Zoo Authority: Chairperson, members, functions, grants
1991.schedulesChanged: Schedule V omitted, Schedule VI added (plants). Wild animal = Schedules I-IV
1991.impact: Major structural amendment. Added plant protection, zoo regulation. Shifted vermin to notification. Increased penalties 12x. Foundation for modern WLPA.

1993.description: Minor amendment extending time limit for Section 38H (zoo recognition) from 6 to 18 months. Repealed 1993 Ordinance.
keyChanges: Extended zoo recognition deadline: 6 months → 18 months (Section 38H proviso)
Repealed Wild Life (Protection) Amendment Ordinance, 1993
Saved actions taken under Ordinance
1993.impact: Technical amendment giving zoos more time for recognition compliance.

2002.description: Landmark amendment - ecological security focus, National/State Boards, Conservation/Community Reserves, NTCA precursor, forfeiture chapter, enhanced penalties.
keyChanges: LONG TITLE CHANGED: 'ensuring ecological and environmental security of the country'
Redefined 'animal' to include ALL chordates and invertebrates
INSERTED Sections 5A, 5B, 5C: National Board for Wild Life (PM Chair, 30+ members)
INSERTED Section 6: State Board for Wild Life (CM Chair, 20+ members)
INSERTED Sections 36A, 36B: Conservation Reserves (govt land, community consultation)
INSERTED Sections 36C, 36D: Community Reserves (private/community land, owner consent)
Central Govt can declare sanctuaries/National Parks (Section 38)
Chapter VIA (Sections 58A-58Y): Forfeiture of property from illegal hunting/trade
Competent Authority, Appellate Tribunal, Administrator for forfeiture
Burden of proof on accused for illegally acquired property
Enhanced penalties: Section 51 - Schedule I/II: ₹10,000 (was ₹25,000); General: ₹25,000 (was ₹10,000)
Section 54: Compounding up to ₹50,000 (was ₹25,000)
Section 60A: Reward 50% of fine (was 20%)
Section 60B: State Govt reward up to ₹10,000 (NEW)
Simplified Schedule references: removed 'Part II of Schedule II' throughout
New definitions: forest officer, forest produce, protected area, National Board, livestock
Taxidermy definition expanded
2002.schedulesChanged: Part II of Schedule II references removed. Vermin = Section 62 notification only.
2002.impact: Most comprehensive amendment. Added participatory governance (Boards), new protected area categories (Conservation/Community Reserves), forfeiture regime, ecological security mandate. Foundation for NTCA (2006).

2006.description: Tiger-focused amendment. Created National Tiger Conservation Authority (NTCA), Tiger Reserves, Tiger Conservation Foundation, Wildlife Crime Control Bureau. Enhanced tiger reserve penalties.
keyChanges: INSERTED Chapter IVB (Sections 38K-38X): National Tiger Conservation Authority
NTCA: Minister Chair, 8 experts, Secretaries, CWLWs rotation, IG Forests Member-Secretary
Tiger Conservation Plan: Core (inviolate) + Buffer (co-existence), ecological corridors
Voluntary relocation with consent, rights settlement, rehabilitation package
Tiger Conservation Foundation per reserve: eco-development, eco-tourism, funding
No boundary alteration without NTCA + National Board approval
No de-notification without NTCA + National Board approval
INSERTED Chapter IVC (Sections 38Y-38Z): Wildlife Crime Control Bureau (WCCB)
WCCB: Centralized wildlife crime intelligence, inter-state/international coordination
Section 51C: SPECIAL TIGER RESERVE PENALTIES - Core area/hunting: 3-7 years, ₹50K-2L (1st), 7 years, ₹5-50L (repeat)
Abetment of Section 51C offence = same punishment
Section 55: WCCB officers can file complaints
Section 63: Rule-making for NTCA/WCCB
Section 64: State rule-making for NTCA
Renamed 'Tiger and Other Endangered Species' to 'Wild Life' in Chapter IVC heading (later 2022)
2006.impact: Institutionalized tiger conservation. Created NTCA (statutory), WCCB (enforcement), tiger reserve legal framework. Core-buffer model. Voluntary relocation with rights. Major enforcement boost.

2022.description: CITES implementation, rationalized schedules, invasive alien species, conservation reserve by Central Govt, voluntary surrender, enhanced penalties, Management/Scientific Authorities.
keyChanges: LONG TITLE: 'conservation, protection and management of wild life'
INSERTED Chapter VB (Sections 49D-49R): CITES Implementation - International Trade Regulation
Schedule IV = CITES Appendices I, II, III species
Management Authority (Section 49E): Additional DG Forests rank - permits, reports
Scientific Authority (Section 49F): Research institutes - non-detriment findings
Export/Import/Re-export/Introduction from sea permits (Sections 49H-49L)
Possession/transfer/breeding of Schedule IV living animals: registration (Section 49M)
Breeding Appendix I species: licence from CWLW (Sections 49N-49O)
Section 42A: VOLUNTARY SURRENDER of captive animals/ivory - no compensation, cert cancelled
Section 43: Captive elephant transport conditions prescribed by Central Govt
Section 38(2A): CENTRAL GOVT CAN DECLARE CONSERVATION RESERVES
Section 62: VERMIN ONLY FROM SCHEDULE II (was Schedules III-V)
Section 62A: INVASIVE ALIEN SPECIES regulation/prohibition (NEW)
Section 62B: Central Govt directions to States for implementation (NEW)
Section 51: ENHANCED PENALTIES - General: ₹1 lakh (was ₹25K); Schedule I/II/Appendix I: ₹25K (was ₹10K); Repeat: ₹5 lakh (was ₹25K)
Section 54: Compounding up to ₹5 lakh (was ₹50K)
Section 35(3A): Interim protection on National Park declaration intent
Section 35(3B): Alternative arrangements for affected persons
Section 29: 'National Board' for sanctuary management in Scheduled Areas
Section 33: 'Manage and protect' per management plans, Gram Sabha consultation
Section 24/25: Land Acquisition Act 1894 → RFCTLARR Act 2013
Section 28: Photography/film-making allowed without habitat change
Section 36D: Community reserve committee for private land (owner + Forest Dept + Panchayat)
Section 38XA: Chapter IVC provisions additional to sanctuary/NP provisions
Chapter IVC renamed: 'Tiger and Other Endangered Species' → 'Wild Life'
Section 38I: Conservation breeding centre exemption
Section 39(4)-(5): Live animals → zoo/rescue centre; disposal no commercial sale
Section 50: Added Management Authority, customs, coast guard officers
Section 55: Added Management Authority, WCCB officers for cognizance
Section 57: 'Wild animal, captive animal' + 'scheduled specimen' in presumptions
Section 61: Power to 'amend any Schedule or add'
Section 63: Extensive rule-making for Chapter VB (CITES)
2022.schedulesChanged: COMPLETE RESTRUCTURE: Schedule I & II (animals), Schedule III (animals), Schedule IV (CITES), Schedule V (vermin), Schedule VI (plants). Part II of Schedule II REMOVED entirely.
2022.impact: CITES compliance. Rationalized schedules (removed confusing Part II). Central Govt conservation reserve power. Invasive species regulation. Voluntary surrender. Major penalty enhancement (4-20x). Elephant transport rules. Interim NP protection.

conservationReserve.oldProvision: Only State Govt could declare on govt land with community consultation
conservationReserve.newProvision: Central Govt can also declare if Section 36A conditions met
conservationReserve.reason: Strengthen conservation in areas where State Govt may not act
conservationReserve.impact: More areas can be protected as conservation reserves

nationalTigerConservationAuthority.enhancedBy: 2022 Amendment (renamed Chapter IVC, Section 38L Member-Secretary rank)
nationalTigerConservationAuthority.oldProvision: Project Tiger was administrative scheme, no statutory authority
nationalTigerConservationAuthority.newProvision: Statutory NTCA with powers to approve plans, disallow ecologically unsustainable land use, direct States
nationalTigerConservationAuthority.reason: Tiger crisis (Sariska, Panna) showed need for statutory authority
nationalTigerConservationAuthority.impact: Legal backbone for tiger conservation. Core-buffer model. Voluntary relocation framework.

citESTradeRegulation.oldProvision: No domestic CITES implementation. EXIM policy handled trade.
citESTradeRegulation.newProvision: Full CITES implementation: Management Authority, Scientific Authority, permit system, registration, breeding licences
citESTradeRegulation.reason: India's CITES obligations. Prevent illegal international trade.
citESTradeRegulation.impact: Legal framework for CITES permits. Appendix I breeding regulated. International trade monitored.

verminDeclaration.oldProvision: Any wild animal except Schedule I/II could be declared vermin (Schedules III-V)
verminDeclaration.newProvision: Only Schedule II species can be declared vermin
verminDeclaration.reason: Prevent misuse of vermin declaration for protected species
verminDeclaration.impact: Stronger protection - Schedule III-V species cannot be declared vermin

penalties.2022: General: ₹1 lakh; Schedule I/II/Appendix I: ₹25K; Repeat: ₹5 lakh; Compounding: ₹5 lakh
penalties.trend: Consistent 4-20x increases per amendment. Deterrence focus.

keyQuestions.whatChangedIn1991: Added plant protection (Chapter IIIA, Schedule VI), Central Zoo Authority (Chapter IVA), redefined wild animal (Schedules I-IV), omitted Schedule V, enhanced penalties 12x, strict bail (51A).
keyQuestions.whatChangedIn2002: Ecological security mandate, National/State Boards (5A-5C), Conservation/Community Reserves (36A-36D), Forfeiture Chapter (58A-58Y), Central Govt sanctuary/NP power, reward system, simplified schedules.
keyQuestions.whatChangedIn2006: NTCA (Chapter IVB), Tiger Reserves (38V), Tiger Conservation Foundation (38X), WCCB (Chapter IVC), special tiger penalties (51C), voluntary relocation framework.
keyQuestions.whatChangedIn2022: CITES implementation (Chapter VB), Schedule IV for CITES, Management/Scientific Authorities, Central Govt conservation reserve, invasive alien species (62A), voluntary surrender (42A), vermin only Schedule II, penalties 4-20x, elephant transport rules, interim NP protection.
